title: Moana 2
tagline: Back on the water. Bring coconuts.
about: Moana sails out with a new crew to break a storm god's curse and reconnect the islands.
cue: Serve the snacks when the Kakamora come paddling up.
faces: Prawns crumbed in shredded coconut and panko, fried
Paper thin taro fried crisp and tossed with sea salt
Snapper marinated in coconut, lime and chilli, grilled in banana leaf
the welcome feast back home on Motunui
Set coconut milk pudding in cups, topped with diced mango
Coconut water, pineapple, lime and honey blended with ice
"Pack the coconuts and the taro, Pua. It's a long paddle tonight, and Maui keeps pinching the fish before it's cooked."
Serve the snacks when the Kakamora come paddling up.

Hot food, full crew. Prices subject to change. Laser issue, fleet standard. Form G-24, sheet 2 of 2. 2024. All drinks alcohol free. Crew notes: Heihei riding along again. Pua the pig in the canoe. Maui's magic fish hook.

    StartersKakamora coconut prawnsPrawns crumbed in shredded coconut and panko, friedHow to make it500g green prawns2 eggs, beaten80g shredded coconut60g panko breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying120ml sweet chilli sauce2 limesPeel the prawns, leaving the tails on.Mix the coconut with the panko.Dip the prawns in beaten egg, then press into the coconut mix.Fry in the oil at 180°C in batches until golden.Stir lime juice into the sweet chilli sauce and serve for dipping.Motunui taro chipsPaper thin taro fried crisp and tossed with sea saltHow to make it600g taro1 L vegetable oil, for frying1 tsp sea salt flakes1/2 tsp chilli flakesPeel the taro and slice very thin on a mandoline.Rinse and dry well.Fry in the oil at 170°C in batches until crisp and pale golden.Toss straight away with sea salt and chilli flakes.MainsOcean voyage fishSnapper marinated in coconut, lime and chilli, grilled in banana leafHow to make it4 snapper fillets800ml coconut milk3 limes2 red chillies, chopped4 banana leaves300g jasmine rice100ml water1 tsp saltMarinate the snapper in some of the coconut milk with the lime juice and chopped red chillies.Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water.Wrap each fillet in a leaf.Grill the parcels.Cook the rice in the remaining coconut milk with the water and salt.Serve the fish in its leaf.Motunui banana leaf pulled porkThe welcome feast back home on MotunuiHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork shoulder rubbed with salt, garlic and brown sugar, slow roasted in banana leaves until it pulls apart, with charred pineapple and coconut slaw.Rub a 2kg pork shoulder with 2 tsp salt, 4 crushed garlic cloves and 2 tbsp brown sugar.Wrap in banana leaves, then foil, and roast at 150°C for 5 hours.Pull apart with forks and toss in the juices.Grill 8 pineapple rings until charred.Toss half a shredded cabbage and 1 grated carrot with 3 tbsp coconut cream, the juice of 1 lime and coriander.Serve together.SweetsHaupia coconut pudding with mangoSet coconut milk pudding in cups, topped with diced mangoHow to make it800ml coconut milk100g caster sugar5 tbsp cornflour2 mangoes30g shredded coconutWhisk the coconut milk, sugar and cornflour over low heat until thick and glossy.Pour into cups.Chill until set.Toast the shredded coconut in a dry pan.Dice the mango and top the puddings with mango and toasted coconut.DrinksPineapple coconut water slushieCoconut water, pineapple, lime and honey blended with iceHow to make it500ml chilled coconut water1 small pineapple1 lime2 tbsp honey4 sprigs of mint2 cups iceCut the pineapple into chunks and keep four wedges for garnish.Blend the coconut water, pineapple, lime juice, honey and ice until smooth and slushy.Pour into glasses or hollowed coconut shells, garnish with a pineapple wedge and mint and serve with straws.
